question: What is labor induction?

options.A: Manually turning a breech baby before the water breaks
options.B: Starting uterine contractions before labor begins naturally
options.C: Speeding up weak contractions after labor has started
options.D: Surgically delivering a baby through an abdominal incision

explanation: Induction means starting the labor process artificially when the woman is not yet in spontaneous labor. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T1#BMP311_U3_T1_h1)

question: When is a midwife performing labor augmentation instead of induction?

options.A: When giving medicine to start labor for a pregnancy that is post-dates
options.B: When scheduling a primary caesarean section for a client with severe pre-eclampsia
options.C: When helping a woman whose spontaneous labor contractions are too weak to progress
options.D: When performing an artificial rupture of membranes to begin the first stage of labor

explanation: Augmentation is used to assist labor that has already started naturally but needs help to move forward. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T1#BMP311_U3_T1_h1)

question: At what gestational age is a pregnancy considered post-term and an indication for induction?
explanation: Pregnancies lasting beyond 42 weeks carry higher risks of placental issues, making induction necessary. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T1#BMP311_U3_T1_h2)

question: A first-time mother arrives at 41 weeks with normal fetal heart tones and a closed, firm cervix. What is the best management plan?

options.A: Evaluate for formal labor induction due to post-dates pregnancy
options.B: Discharge home and advise return only when she feels painful contractions
options.C: Perform an immediate emergency caesarean section without delay
options.D: Prescribe tocolytic drugs to prolong the pregnancy for another week

explanation: A pregnancy reaching 41 to 42 weeks without spontaneous labor is a standard reason to evaluate for induction to prevent fetal complications. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T1#BMP311_U3_T1_h2)

question: What does a high Bishop score tell us about the cervix?

options.A: It shows that the fetus is lying in a transverse breech position
options.B: It is favorable and ready for successful induction
options.C: It is completely closed and firm, requiring mechanical ripening
options.D: It indicates an absolute contraindication to any vaginal delivery

explanation: A high Bishop score means the cervix is soft, thinned out, and open, predicting a good chance of a successful vaginal birth. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T1#BMP311_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why is calculating a Bishop score important before starting an oxytocin infusion?

options.A: It prevents the occurrence of postpartum hemorrhage after delivery
options.B: It detects the presence of meconium-stained amniotic fluid early
options.C: It directly measures the exact weight of the developing fetus in utero
options.D: It helps decide if cervical ripening agents are needed before oxytocin

explanation: An unfavorable Bishop score means oxytocin alone will likely fail, so ripening agents must be used first. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T1#BMP311_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which medication is commonly used for cervical ripening because it is affordable and stable at room temperature?
explanation: Misoprostol is affordable and stable, making it a popular choice for cervical ripening in many clinical settings. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T1#BMP311_U3_T1_h4)

question: How do mechanical dilators like the transcervical Foley catheter help prepare the cervix?

options.A: By lowering the maternal blood pressure to prevent dangerous eclamptic seizures
options.B: By dissolving the fetal membranes to cause an immediate rush of amniotic fluid
options.C: By directly stopping all uterine contractions to give the uterine muscle adequate rest
options.D: By exerting direct physical pressure that opens the cervical canal and releases local prostaglandins

explanation: Mechanical methods work through physical stretch and promote local prostaglandin release to soften and open the cervix. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T1#BMP311_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of an amniotomy during labor?

options.A: Measuring the exact internal temperature of the amniotic cavity
options.B: Surgically repairing an old perineal tear from a previous delivery
options.C: Artificially rupturing the amniotic membranes to release fluid and stimulate contractions
options.D: Administering intravenous fluids to prevent maternal dehydration during the first stage

explanation: Amniotomy involves breaking the bag of waters to release fluid and help start or speed up labor. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T1#BMP311_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the most critical action a midwife must take right after performing an amniotomy?

options.A: Check the fetal heart rate to ensure there is no sign of cord compression
options.B: Document the total fluid intake and urine output for the past four hours
options.C: Perform a strict bimanual pelvic examination to measure exact cervical effacement
options.D: Assist the mother to stand up and walk around the delivery ward corridor

explanation: Checking the fetal heart rate immediately after membranes rupture is vital to catch sudden cord prolapse or distress early. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T1#BMP311_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the safest way to give an intravenous oxytocin infusion during labor?

options.A: Giving rapid manual bolus injections every fifteen minutes
options.B: Adding the medication directly into a primary saline bag without a pump
options.C: Using an electronic infusion pump connected to a secondary line
options.D: Mixing the drug into an intramuscular suspension for slow release

explanation: An infusion pump ensures precise control over the small doses of oxytocin needed to prevent dangerous overdose. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T1#BMP311_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why must oxytocin dose increases be done slowly and at scheduled intervals?

options.A: To make sure the intravenous cannula does not slip out of the vein
options.B: To prevent uterine hyperstimulation and protect the baby from lack of oxygen
options.C: To ensure the placenta absorbs all the medicine before contractions start
options.D: To allow the mother enough time to eat a full meal during labor

explanation: Slow increases prevent the uterus from contracting too strongly or too often, which can cut off oxygen to the fetus. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T1#BMP311_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the very first action a midwife should take when uterine hyperstimulation happens during an oxytocin infusion?

options.A: Administer a dose of oral misoprostol
options.B: Prepare the client for immediate discharge

explanation: Stopping the oxytocin removes the trigger for the excessive contractions, protecting the fetus from low oxygen levels. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T1#BMP311_U3_T1_h7)

question: A woman receiving oxytocin has contractions lasting 90 seconds with short rest periods, and the fetal heart rate drops. Which nursing action helps improve blood flow to the baby best?

options.A: Applying gentle abdominal pressure to slow down the breathing
options.B: Turning the woman onto her left side and stopping the oxytocin
options.C: Walking the woman up and down the hospital corridor
options.D: Instructing the woman to push forcefully with every contraction

explanation: The left side-lying position relieves pressure on major blood vessels, increases blood flow, and improves oxygen delivery to the fetus. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T1#BMP311_U3_T1_h7)
